Bramblewood Effects Lab

Every animation, light, shader and sound in the game so far, live. Cards here use the game's own stylesheet and art. Hover the foil cards, press the buttons, and use headphones for the sound section. Status: Live in the game, Partly built, Idea not built yet.

Combat skills new

Choreographed skill effects. Arrow and Fire Arrow are now live in the game with this exact animation: the archer draws (leans back while the arrow is pulled along the line of fire), releases with a snap-forward recoil and a bowstring ring, the arrow arcs and accelerates, then sticks and quivers as the target is knocked back. The rest are new prototypes for skills we have, ready to wire in.

Procedural damage & GSAP experiments New

From bramblewood-procfx.js (ProcFX). Stone fractures dug by drunken-miner random walks, a cellular automaton that erodes a castle into falling rubble, and a procedurally aged “cards of old” finish. Everything is seeded: the same castle or card always breaks and ages the same way. Then five GSAP experiments: Voronoi shatter, a Flip riffle, a quickTo lantern, a scrubbable forge timeline and a grid ripple.

Drunken-miner cracks New

🏰
Castle
❤30

Click the castle to strike it there. Each hit sends out “miners”: random walks with momentum and sharp kinks that taper and branch, drawn with a dark gap, a shadowed core and a lit lower lip so they read as chiselled stone. A strike spalls a small crater. Calling it again keeps the old cracks and adds new ones.

ProcFX.cracks · ProcFX.castleDamage(el, hp/max)

Cellular-automaton crumble New

🏰
Castle
❤30

A grid of jittered stone blocks over the tile. Each step a block breaks away with a chance that rises with its broken neighbours, along the cracks, and sharply when the block under it is gone. Fallen blocks leave the tile's mask and drop as rubble that bounces; broken edges get a dark rim with a lit lip.

ProcFX.crumble · castle kill

An aged-paper finish grown per card: yellowed paper browning toward the edges, fibre grain and specks, foxing spots and a water stain with a darker tide line (both grown by a cellular automaton), drunken-walk creases with flaked ink along them, a dog-eared corner, rubbed white edges and corners, faded ink and an old halftone print. A soft warm sheen follows the light. Hover a card.

Damage numbers new

Each number bursts out of the hit, then recoils back to size; the burst behind it fades fast. An icon in front says what kind of hit it was. On the enemy row numbers pop higher on the card; on yours they spread out more sideways. Press a button to hit the card.

Music Live

Every note is composed or generated here and played by small synthesised instruments, so the whole library is ours: no samples, no licences, nothing to download. Use headphones.
